name: es31-separate-vertex-format
title: Separate vertex format and vertex buffer bindings
summary: glVertexAttribFormat / glVertexAttribIFormat / glVertexAttribBinding / glBindVertexBuffer / glVertexBindingDivisor: one binding (with a binding offset and relative offsets) feeding three attributes, a binding re-pointed to another buffer and stride without touching the formats, two bindings with divisor 0 and 1 (then 2), an attribute moved to another binding, exact pure integer formats, the legacy glVertexAttribPointer / glVertexAttribDivisor as shorthand for the same state (queried through VERTEX_ATTRIB_BINDING, RELATIVE_OFFSET and VERTEX_BINDING_BUFFER/OFFSET/STRIDE/DIVISOR), the limits MAX_VERTEX_ATTRIB_BINDINGS / RELATIVE_OFFSET / STRIDE in use, and every error including the default vertex array object; twelve cells compared with a CPU model that fetches from the same bytes.
spec: ES 3.2 §10.3.1 Specifying Arrays for Generic Vertex Attributes (Table 10.3, VertexAttribFormat, VertexAttribIFormat, BindVertexBuffer, VertexAttribBinding, the equivalence of VertexAttribPointer, errors)
ES 3.2 §10.3.3 Transferring Array Elements (missing components), §10.3.7 Vertex Arrays in Buffer Objects (offset + relativeoffset + i * stride)
ES 3.2 §10.4 Vertex Array Objects, §10.5 Drawing Commands Using Vertex Arrays (instance element index)
ES 3.2 §10.6 Vertex Array and Vertex Array Object Queries, §10.7 Required State (initial binding stride 16)
ES 3.2 §2.2.2 Data Conversions For State Query Commands, §2.3.1 Errors, §20.1 Simple Queries (indexed state)
ES 3.2 Table 21.3 Vertex Array Object State, Table 21.42 and 21.44 (MAX_VERTEX_ATTRIB_BINDINGS / RELATIVE_OFFSET / STRIDE, MAX_VERTEX_ATTRIBS)
GLSL ES 3.00 §4.3.4 Input Variables, §4.3.8.1 Input Layout Qualifiers (layout(location))

api.glVertexAttribFormat: size/type/normalized/relativeoffset of float, normalized UNSIGNED_BYTE and normalized SHORT attributes (relative offsets 0, 8, 12, up to the limit) observed in the pixels; state read back (SIZE, TYPE, NORMALIZED, INTEGER, RELATIVE_OFFSET, BINDING unchanged); INVALID_VALUE (attribindex, size 0/5, relativeoffset MAX+1), INVALID_ENUM, INVALID_OPERATION (packed type with size 3, default VAO); a failed call changes nothing
api.glVertexAttribIFormat: UNSIGNED_BYTE x2, INT and SHORT attributes arrive exactly (2^24 + 1 and -3, the band turns red otherwise); INTEGER flag read back; FLOAT / HALF_FLOAT / packed -> INVALID_ENUM, size 5, relativeoffset MAX+1 -> INVALID_VALUE, default VAO -> INVALID_OPERATION
api.glVertexAttribBinding: one binding feeds attributes 0-2, an attribute is moved to binding 2 (pixels), the highest binding indices MAX-1 and MAX-2 are used; VERTEX_ATTRIB_BINDING read back; attribindex / bindingindex out of range -> INVALID_VALUE, default VAO -> INVALID_OPERATION
api.glBindVertexBuffer: buffer, binding offset (24, 8, 0, 4096; also above 2^32) and stride (16, 24, 12, 8, 4, MAX_VERTEX_ATTRIB_STRIDE) fetch the pixels; re-pointing a binding without any format call changes the picture; VERTEX_BINDING_BUFFER / OFFSET / STRIDE and VERTEX_ATTRIB_ARRAY_BUFFER_BINDING read back; errors: bindingindex, negative offset or stride, stride MAX+1, never generated or deleted buffer name (INVALID_OPERATION), default VAO; a failed call changes nothing; a generated but never bound name is valid
api.glVertexBindingDivisor: divisor 1 and 2 on the binding that feeds the color and offset attributes: instances advance together or in pairs (pixels); VERTEX_BINDING_DIVISOR and VERTEX_ATTRIB_ARRAY_DIVISOR of every attribute on the binding read back; bindingindex = MAX -> INVALID_VALUE, default VAO -> INVALID_OPERATION
api.glVertexAttribPointer: defines attributes 0-2 of two VAOs (pixels); afterwards VERTEX_ATTRIB_BINDING = index, RELATIVE_OFFSET reset to 0, VERTEX_BINDING_BUFFER/OFFSET/STRIDE (effective stride from stride 0), VERTEX_ATTRIB_ARRAY_STRIDE keeps the argument, the divisor of the binding is unchanged; it overrides an earlier glVertexAttribBinding/glBindVertexBuffer of the same attribute
api.glVertexAttribIPointer: sets INTEGER 1, binding = index and the effective stride 4 (UNSIGNED_SHORT x2), read back
api.glVertexAttribDivisor: equivalent to glVertexAttribBinding(i, i) + glVertexBindingDivisor(i, d): BINDING becomes i, VERTEX_BINDING_DIVISOR[i] = d, the previously used binding keeps its divisor
api.glEnableVertexAttribArray: arrays 0-5 enabled in the VAOs whose pixels are compared
api.glGetVertexAttribiv: VERTEX_ATTRIB_BINDING, RELATIVE_OFFSET, ARRAY_SIZE/TYPE/NORMALIZED/INTEGER/STRIDE/DIVISOR/BUFFER_BINDING after each command above and the initial values of a fresh VAO
api.glGetVertexAttribPointerv: VERTEX_ATTRIB_ARRAY_POINTER is the byte offset passed to glVertexAttribPointer (24, 40)
api.glGetIntegeri_v: VERTEX_BINDING_BUFFER / STRIDE / DIVISOR / OFFSET of indexed bindings (fresh VAO: 0, 16, 0, 0; after commands); index = MAX_VERTEX_ATTRIB_BINDINGS -> INVALID_VALUE; a 64-bit offset is clamped to INT_MAX (known Mesa deviation)
api.glGetInteger64i_v: VERTEX_BINDING_OFFSET (64-bit state, Table 21.3): 0, 4096, and 2^33 + 8 (known Mesa deviation: low 32 bits only)
api.glGetIntegerv: MAX_VERTEX_ATTRIBS, MAX_VERTEX_ATTRIB_BINDINGS, MAX_VERTEX_ATTRIB_RELATIVE_OFFSET and MAX_VERTEX_ATTRIB_STRIDE compared with their minimum values and used by the limit cells and the error checks
api.glGenVertexArrays: ten VAOs: eight drawn, one fresh (defaults, isolation), one scratch for the state and error checks
api.glBindVertexArray: selects the vertex state of each cell; the default VAO makes the new commands INVALID_OPERATION
api.glGenBuffers: fourteen data buffers plus four names used only in state and error checks
api.glBindBuffer: ARRAY_BUFFER for the legacy glVertexAttribPointer calls; a name is bound once to create a buffer that is then deleted for the INVALID_OPERATION check
api.glBufferData: vertex data observed through the rendered pixels (CPU model reads the same bytes)
api.glDeleteBuffers: cleanup; a deleted name passed to glBindVertexBuffer -> INVALID_OPERATION
api.glDrawArrays: TRIANGLES from every non-instanced cell; pixels match the CPU model
api.glDrawArraysInstanced: TRIANGLE_STRIP x4 instances with binding divisor 1, 2 and with an attribute on another binding
api.glUseProgram: float and integer programs select the cells
api.glGetUniformLocation: u_scale, u_expect_cell, u_expect_big, u_expect_neg located; effects observed in the pixels
api.glUniform1i: u_expect_big / u_expect_neg: the integer band turns red when the expectation is wrong (negative control)
api.glUniform2f: u_scale places instanced quads; matches the model
api.glUniform2ui: u_expect_cell compared with the uvec2 attribute in the shader
api.glViewport: per-cell viewports map NDC to the probed pixels
api.glClearColor: background pixels equal the clear color
api.glDisable: DITHER off for exact color writes
api.glReadPixels: RGBA/UNSIGNED_BYTE readback of every cell (through demo::read_rgba8)

visual_review.notes: Viewed the gpu and llvmpipe captures (256x256); the zink capture differs from gpu in 41 edge pixels (compare with 2% fuzz). Top row: a Gouraud triangle (red/green/blue corners) displaced per vertex through the SHORT offset; the inverted yellow/cyan/magenta triangle of buffer B (re-pointed binding, stride 24); four squares (red, green bottom; blue, yellow top) for divisor 1; only the bottom pair (red, green) for divisor 2. Middle row: four squares on a diagonal (offset attribute on binding 2); three green bands (every integer arrived exactly); the legacy red/green/blue triangle; the same colors on L2's positions (re-pointed binding 0). Bottom row: the legacy triangle shifted by buffer Y; orange/teal/purple triangle (two bindings on one buffer); white/red/blue triangle (bindings MAX-1, MAX-2); yellow/cyan/magenta triangle (stride 2048, relative offset 2044). Background is the dark-blue clear color; no stray marks.
